intents.q: What is the Bloc Crash Course?
intents.a: A live, one-weekend course: 2 sessions, about 5 hours. You learn Bloc the way real Flutter teams use it and build a login screen, a product list from an API and a shopping cart, with tests, pushed to your GitHub. The current fee, dates and seats are shown live on the course page.

intents.q: What's in the Bloc Crash Course?
intents.a: Session 1, Bloc foundations: why state management, Cubit, Bloc with events, BlocListener and BlocConsumer, immutable states with Equatable. You build a login screen with loading and error states. Session 2, Bloc in a real app: the repository pattern, a product list from a REST API, a cart shared across screens, testing with bloc_test and mocktail, a folder structure that scales, and reviewing AI-written Bloc code.

intents.q: Who is the Bloc Crash Course for?
intents.a: It's the next step after Flutter basics, not a beginner course. You need widgets, StatefulWidget and setState, and a little async Dart (Future, async/await). You don't need to know Bloc: we start it from zero. Totally new to Flutter? Start with Flutter in 10 Days.

intents.q: What is the Flutter, Bloc & Clean Architecture course?
intents.a: A live course over 3 weekends: 6 sessions, about 15 hours. You learn Dart OOP, clean architecture, Bloc and testing by building a ball-by-ball cricket scorer app, then ship a release APK and a GitHub project you can explain in interviews. The current fee, dates and seats are shown live on the course page.

intents.q: What's in the Clean Architecture course?
intents.a: 1) Dart OOP through the game: classes, encapsulation, immutable objects. 2) Polymorphism and the rules of cricket: sealed classes, pattern matching, SOLID, test-first rules. 3) Clean architecture: layers, use cases, repositories, get_it. 4) Bloc in depth: every ball is an event, undo, BlocListener. 5) Scorecard and history, sharing, bloc_test. 6) Ship it: release APK, README, explaining your architecture, reviewing AI-written code.

intents.q: Who is the Clean Architecture course for?
intents.a: People who can already build Flutter screens and want to build them properly. You need Flutter basics and a little Dart; we cover the OOP you need in session 1. You only need cricket basics (runs, overs, wides, wickets). Did the Bloc Crash Course? This goes much further: OOP, architecture, dependency injection, saving data and testing a whole app.
